findings.text: the embed_text lambda returns item['description'] for a generated row, so a generated row whose feed description is empty lands in the writer's empty-text arm, which nulls its stored vector and stamps the empty-text hash; that contradicts the comment at :283 that such a row's vector is left untouched, and the row leaves vector search until the re-embed sweep.

the generated_state hash override has no test: the repeat-import node in tests/graph/test_controls_metadata.py:57 carries no generated_description, so deleting this block would leave every graph test green while a source import would again re-report and re-embed every generated row on each run.

the reembed_stale_signal_descriptions docstring still says the sweep rewrites with 'the description-only embed text, so the stored vector, its hash and its description move together', while embed_text now prefers the generated text and embed_only writes no description property at all, so the docstring misdescribes the mechanism the same commit changed.

assert row['description'] == 'Plasma current' compares the captured item against the literal the test itself passed in, so it holds whatever the writer does and survives a regression in the slot it appears to guard; the statement assertions at :241-243 are the ones that actually catch a revert to s.description.

the pre-repair feed-marker total (2,708) is derived by subtracting 190 from the post-repair 2,898 rather than measured, so the claim that no other row changed rests on that arithmetic; the done_when asks for the graph total before, and a measurement taken before the first mutation would have settled it.
